signals.signal: Corporate Presentation - June 2026 (new deck, not seen in prior runs) states plainly why Malta is a technology opportunity: 'HSBC Malta needs a restart' - 'Over a decade of operations under non-core status', 'Underinvested in IT and personnel', 'Reshape operational processes'; and lists among the synergies 'Cost and efficiency optimisation (in-sourcing, tech investments, modernisation, digitalisation)'. Malta stand-alone FY2025: net loans EUR 2.8bn, deposits EUR 6.5bn, assets EUR 8.2bn, 923 FTEs, C/I 55%; combined group pro-forma assets EUR 16.4bn.
signals.implies: The acquirer's own investment case is that the target is IT-underinvested and must be re-platformed and in-sourced away from HSBC group systems. This is the single strongest buying signal in the file: channels/self-service, cash automation, digital onboarding/eKYC, AML/compliance, transaction monitoring, HSM/security and managed services all in scope for a 12-branch, EUR 8.2bn bank inside 2026-2027.
signals.likelihood: Vendor decisions during operational-readiness phase, i.e. H2-2026 to Q1-2027
signals.followup: Get into the Malta target-operating-model workstream via CrediaBank Athens (COO/CIO office), not via Valletta; ask which HSBC-group services are being replaced vs in-sourced.

signals.signal: HSBC Malta acquisition roadmap in the June-2026 deck, now with completion status per milestone: December 2025 SPA signed (Completed); January 2026 file submitted to the local regulator (MFSA, Completed); April 2026 finalisation of the target operating model (Completed); Q4 2026 regulatory approval from the local regulator and the ECB on the change of control, plus finalisation of operational readiness (Ongoing); April 2027 legal/operational merger together with the change of ownership (Legal Day 1).
signals.implies: The target operating model is already finalised (April 2026) and operational readiness is the live workstream. Technology procurement for Malta is happening NOW, between now and April 2027 - engaging after Legal Day 1 is too late. Confirms the April-2027 Legal Day 1 in the baseline and adds the April-2026 TOM completion, which the baseline did not have.
signals.likelihood: Operational-readiness build running through Q4-2026 / Q1-2027
signals.followup: Request the TOM's technology-domain map; identify which of channels/cards/ATM management/eKYC/AML/monitoring are being bought vs built.

signals.signal: HSBC Malta FY2025 accounts (approved 25/02/2026): operating costs up 6% to EUR 119.9m, including a notable item of EUR 3.1m for accelerated amortisation of software 'following a revision to estimated useful lives in anticipation of the prospective transfer to CrediaBank'. Same statement confirms 2025 delivered SEPA Instant payments, an IT-infrastructure upgrade and 'completing the replacement of our ATM fleet across Malta and Gozo'. PBT EUR 109.0m, PAT EUR 71.6m, EPS 19.9c.
signals.source_name: HSBC Bank Malta company announcement HSBC474 (Malta Stock Exchange)
signals.implies: Confirms with hard accounting evidence that HSBC-group software will be decommissioned at separation. Also an important negative qualifier: the ATM hardware itself was just replaced across Malta and Gozo during 2025, so the Malta opening is software, cash automation in branch, AML/monitoring and managed services rather than new ATM boxes.
signals.likelihood: Software replacement is contractually unavoidable at separation
signals.followup: Identify the OEM and the managed-services holder of the 2025 Malta/Gozo ATM fleet replacement - that contract will be re-papered at change of control.

signals.signal: Q1-2026 interim directors' statement (05/05/2026): PBT EUR 21.3m, -24% YoY; costs up EUR 3.7m (12%) YoY partly due to 'accelerated amortisation of intangible assets in view of the change in their estimated useful lives'; CEO: 'Continuing to deliver for our customers and shareholders while upgrading digital infrastructure, is our top priority'; transition to new majority shareholder CrediaBank 'progressing', subject to regulatory approval.
signals.source_name: HSBC Bank Malta company announcement HSBC478 (Malta Stock Exchange)
signals.implies: Accelerated software write-down continues into 2026 and the CEO names upgrading digital infrastructure as top priority - an active, budgeted technology programme in Malta while ownership changes hands.
signals.followup: Read the 04/08/2026 H1 accounts for the FY2026 accelerated-amortisation run-rate and any named separation/IT programme cost.

signals.signal: Board of Directors scheduled to meet Tuesday 04/08/2026 to approve H1-2026 interim accounts and consider an interim dividend. No company announcement above HSBC479 had been published as at 30/07/2026 (HSBC480-483 all 404 on the Malta Stock Exchange CDN).
signals.source_name: HSBC Bank Malta company announcement HSBC479 (Malta Stock Exchange)
signals.implies: Next hard datapoint on separation cost, software amortisation and the transaction timetable. Diary item for the Malta pursuit.
signals.followup: Pull HSBC480+ from cdn.borzamalta.com.mt on 05/08/2026.

signals.signal: 1st 'New Experience' branch in Thessaloniki opened 04/02/2026 at Tsimiski 8. The primary release itemises the technology: TCR (teller cash recycler) machines to speed teller cash transactions, customer recognition by bank card at the entrance, abolition of the traditional counter, remote-service points staffed by CrediaBank representatives via CrediaConnect, and an interactive product-discovery screen driven by moving physical objects, co-developed with the Institute of Computer Science of the Foundation for Research and Technology (FORTH/ITE). Accessibility: sign-language interpretation, Braille documents, neurodiversity and mobility infrastructure; energy-efficient equipment and renewable electricity.
signals.implies: Each New Experience branch is a cash-automation + self-service + video-teller build: Printec cash recyclers/TCRs, branch self-service, VTM/VTS integration, card-based access control, accessibility kit and managed services. The TCR/VTS incumbent is still undisclosed - a standing identification task.
signals.likelihood: Programme already contracted; incremental unit orders through end-2026
signals.followup: Ask CrediaBank retail-network/procurement who supplies the TCRs and VTS endpoints; visit Tsimiski 8 and Panepistimiou to read the OEM badge.

signals.signal: Panepistimiou (Athens, Panepistimiou 19 & Omirou) New Experience branch inaugurated 06/05/2026. Same stack as Thessaloniki and names the remote-transaction points explicitly as 'VTS' delivered through CrediaConnect, alongside TCR machines, card-based entry recognition, counter-less open service spaces and the FORTH/ITE interactive digital product-discovery system.
signals.implies: Confirms VTS/video-teller is a standard element of the concept, not a one-off pilot. Printec VTM/VTS integration, recyclers, entry/queue management and managed services across the refurbishment programme.
signals.likelihood: High - programme is live and publicised branch by branch
signals.followup: Obtain the full 2026 refurbishment schedule (which of the 66 branches, in what order) from the retail-banking GM's team.

signals.signal: CrediaBank's own New Experience branch locator now names eight live branches: Skoufa 3 Athens; Panepistimiou 19 & Omirou Athens; Tsimiski 8 Thessaloniki; Kalamata (Sidirodromikou Stathmou 14 & Antonopoulou); Patra (Othonos-Amalias 37 & Ag. Andreou 28); Tripoli (Ethnikis Antistasis 1); Heraklion 25is Avgoustou 94; Heraklion Knossou Ave 205. A ninth, Chania (Andrea Papandreou 11-13), was inaugurated 28/07/2026 and is not yet on the page. The June-2026 deck states 8 branches completed, 3 additional expected shortly, 40% of the network refurbished planned by end-2026.
signals.source_name: CrediaBank 'New Experience Branches' locator page (primary) + Corporate Presentation June 2026
signals.implies: A named, verifiable target list of installed sites plus roughly 18 more to convert by end-2026 (40% of 66 = c.26). Gives a concrete unit count for a TCR/self-service/VTS proposal and a reference-visit itinerary.
signals.followup: Visit two of the eight and photograph the TCR and VTS units to identify the incumbent OEM; then position replacement/expansion and managed services for the remaining c.18.

signals.signal: Chania (Crete) New Experience branch inaugurated 28/07/2026 at Andrea Papandreou 11-13, described in local press as the third New Experience branch in Crete. Technology named: card-based customer recognition at entry, TCR machines at the teller, counter-less transaction areas, sign-language interpretation, neurodiversity and mobility infrastructure, energy-efficient equipment with electricity fully from renewable sources.
signals.implies: Rollout is accelerating and reaching regional Crete, where CrediaBank inherited the Pancreta footprint. More TCR/self-service units per quarter. Not on the bank's own locator page yet, so press-tier only.
signals.likelihood: Confirmed event; count to be validated at H1 results 06/08/2026
signals.followup: Confirm the Crete/total New Experience count in the H1-2026 release on 06/08/2026.

signals.signal: Euronet Worldwide's Q2-2026 results release, filed as exhibit 99.1 to an 8-K on 30/07/2026, contains no mention of CrediaBank or Greece: the Payments Infrastructure segment reports 57,814 installed and 57,071 active ATMs at 30/06/2026 (both +1% YoY) with cc revenue +10%, but no completed acquisition. The CrediaBank merchant-acquiring and ATM transfer, guided to close in Q3-2026, therefore had NOT closed as at 30/07/2026.
signals.source_name: Euronet Worldwide 8-K exhibit 99.1, Q2-2026 results (SEC EDGAR)
signals.implies: Status change: the foreclosure of CrediaBank Greece ATM/POS is agreed but not yet consummated. There is a narrow window before closing to secure the in-branch cash-automation scope (TCR) explicitly outside the Euronet perimeter, and to clarify whether the 80 in-branch ATMs transfer or stay.
signals.likelihood: Closing expected during Q3-2026; regulatory approval outstanding
signals.followup: Watch Euronet's Q3-2026 8-K (late Oct-2026) and the CrediaBank H1 release for the closing announcement and the exact asset perimeter.

signals.signal: CrediaBank's own release of 12/05/2026 states the fleet and the arrangement in the bank's words: free unlimited withdrawals and balance enquiries for CrediaBank customers at 141 CrediaBank ATMs (80 in-branch, 61 off-site) plus more than 2,500 Euronet ATMs nationwide. Same release restates the footprint: 66 branches, 5 business centres, c.350,000 retail and business customers, 5th-largest Greek bank by assets. Press reporting of the 07/01/2026 definitive agreement puts the combined Euronet-plus-CrediaBank acquiring operation at more than USD 22bn processed annually and over 240,000 merchants.
signals.source_name: CrediaBank press release (PDF, primary); Euronet/GlobeNewswire release 07/01/2026
signals.implies: NEGATIVE and now primary-sourced: the Greek ATM estate (141 units) and merchant acquiring go to Euronet under a 3-year exclusive payments/wallet tie-up. Treat CrediaBank Greece ATM hardware, ATM managed services and POS/acquiring as foreclosed; concentrate on in-branch cash automation (TCR), VTS, eKYC/AML and Malta.
signals.likelihood: Foreclosed for at least 3 years from closing
signals.followup: Establish whether the 80 in-branch ATMs are inside the Euronet perimeter or stay with the bank as branches convert to TCR - that boundary decides whether any in-branch device opportunity survives.

signals.signal: Digital transformation programme status in the June-2026 deck: 'Program successfully launched and fully mobilized across all business and technology streams'; 2026 scope, roadmap and stream priorities finalised; enterprise-wide diagnostic of key omnichannel processes completed with a KPI/value-realisation framework; a 'Digital experience design system' delivered as the foundation for scalable digital capabilities across channels; initial client-experience journeys and new technology platforms delivered into production. The strategic-pillar page states 'Program launched, first deliveries expected in 3Q26' and a cost-to-income ratio 450bps better YoY.
signals.implies: An omnichannel replatforming with named 3Q26 first deliveries. Entry points for Printec digital onboarding/eKYC, channel integration, AML/compliance and managed services alongside whichever integrator holds the programme.
signals.followup: Identify the programme's prime integrator and the platforms behind CrediaBank e-Banking/Mobile and the design system; find the eKYC/identity gap.

signals.signal: eGov-KYC is live in production as a customer-facing self-service journey: the bank's support menu carries a dedicated 'Update of details via eGov-KYC' service, alongside an API Portal, self-service password unlock, card management and device enrolment.
signals.implies: The Greek state eGov-KYC rail is already integrated, so a pure eKYC pitch in Greece is partly closed; the remaining room is remote onboarding for non-residents/Malta, liveness/document verification, and the AML screening and transaction-monitoring layers behind it. The public API Portal is a concrete integration surface.
signals.followup: Check whether eGov-KYC covers onboarding as well as data refresh, and whether Malta will need a separate remote-onboarding stack (no Maltese eGov-KYC equivalent).

signals.signal: Cost and headcount rebase in the June-2026 deck: 66 branches at Q1-2026 versus 77 at Q1-2025 (-14%); 1,204 group FTEs versus 1,408 (-14%) after the voluntary exit scheme; EUR 25m of synergies crystallised from the Pancreta merger, with the deck warning the trend 'will be slightly reversed given the preparatory phase for the Malta transaction'.
signals.implies: Fewer branches and 14% fewer staff serving c.350k customers means transactions must move to machines and remote channels - the structural driver behind TCR, VTS and self-service. Management also signals it will accept a cost increase for Malta preparation, i.e. budget is available for separation-driven technology.
signals.followup: Quantify branch transactions per FTE in the H1 release to size the cash-automation business case.

signals.signal: EIB and CrediaBank signed a facility of up to EUR 100m for security and defence SME/midcap investment, with the first EUR 50m tranche signed. CrediaBank is the first non-systemic bank in Europe and the second bank in Greece admitted to the EIB Security & Defence programme, making Greece the first country with more than one participating financial partner; up to EUR 200m expected to be mobilised. Extends an existing EIB relationship in leasing.
signals.source_name: CrediaBank / EIB joint press release (PDF, primary)
signals.implies: New regulated lending flow into defence-sector counterparties raises sanctions/AML screening, enhanced due diligence and transaction-monitoring requirements. Fits Printec AML/compliance and transaction monitoring, particularly with the Bank of Greece 2026 supervisory priority being on-site inspection of customer transaction-monitoring systems.
signals.followup: Approach CrediaBank compliance/AML on defence-sector EDD and sanctions screening ahead of the BoG 2026 transaction-monitoring inspections.

signals.signal: Strategic partnership announced 16/07/2026 covering investment-strategy design, strategic and tactical asset allocation, model portfolios and fund selection, and investment research. The release states the partnership 'creates the preconditions for the development and distribution of modern digital investment solutions, within CrediaBank's digital-transformation strategy'.
signals.implies: A digital wealth/investment channel requires suitability assessment, digital onboarding/eKYC for investment products and MiFID-grade identity, consent and record-keeping. Fits Printec digital onboarding/eKYC and compliance.
signals.followup: Map who builds the digital investment journey (in-house programme vs integrator) and pitch the identity/eKYC and record-keeping layer.

signals.signal: SPA signed 11/05/2026 for the acquisition of a majority stake in Pantelakis Securities (investment-firm/AEPEY), with the June-2026 deck confirming 70% and describing the move as expansion into brokerage and securities; call/put over the remaining 30% after three years. Alongside the Evropi Holdings general-insurance acquisition (share exchange announced 21/05/2026).
signals.implies: Two more regulated entities (securities firm, insurance) join the group, each with its own onboarding, client-money, suitability, AML screening and transaction-monitoring obligations that will be consolidated onto group platforms. Fits Printec eKYC, AML/compliance and monitoring at group level.
signals.followup: Ask whether AML/monitoring will be consolidated group-wide (bank + brokerage + insurance) - that is the shape of a single larger deal.

signals.signal: 2026 financial calendar amended 18/06/2026: H1-2026 results announcement set for 06/08/2026.
signals.implies: Next hard disclosure of branch count, New Experience refurbishment progress, Euronet closing status and the Malta timetable. Diary item.
signals.followup: Read the H1-2026 release and deck on 06/08/2026.

signals.signal: Thrivest Holding placed 333,333,333 CrediaBank shares (c.16.7%) by accelerated bookbuild on 15/07/2026, reducing its holding to c.24.0%, with UBS, Morgan Stanley, Euroxx and Pantelakis as joint bookrunners and a 90-day lock-up. Follows the EUR 300m share capital increase whose use-of-proceeds filing (07/04/2026) reports gross EUR 300m, issue costs EUR 19.7m including VAT and net proceeds EUR 280.3m applied immediately to strengthen the capital position; Q1-2026 CET1 16.6% and total capital 22.4% pro-forma for the SCI (OCR thresholds are 8.99% CET1 / 13.81% total, correcting the earlier confusion in the baseline).
signals.implies: Capital and free float are in place to fund Malta and the technology programme; there is no capital constraint on 2026-2027 technology procurement. Confirms and corrects the baseline's known-stale CET1/TCR item.
signals.followup: None - context for pricing/scale of proposals.

signals.signal: Planned upgrade of digital services: CrediaBank e-Banking and CrediaBank Mobile taken out of service for maintenance windows Saturday 07/02 23:45-03:00 and Sunday 08/02 04:30-08:00 (2026).
signals.implies: Concrete evidence that the digital-channel replatforming is landing in production, i.e. active integration work around e-banking and mobile. Minor but useful timing signal for channel integration and managed services.
signals.followup: Identify the digital-channel platform vendor behind CrediaBank e-Banking/Mobile and the 'Digital experience design system'.

signals.signal: Board change announced 30/07/2026: a new non-executive director elected to replace a resigning member, with the board re-constituted. Latest item on the bank's press office as at 30/07/2026.
signals.implies: Governance housekeeping only; no direct product implication. Logged so the run's coverage of the press office is complete through 30/07/2026.
signals.followup: None.

coverage_notes: Not resumed from a JSON checkpoint - the .json did not exist, but an interrupted-run .md from 15:49 today was present; every claim it carried was re-derived from primary sources this run rather than copied, and several new items were found on top of it. Angles used: (1) crediabank.com sitemap.xml enumerated with a desktop UA, giving all 58 press/ATHEX items of 2026 with lastmod dates, each opened and its /media/*.pdf extracted locally with pdfminer.six - this surfaced two items no prior run had: the Thessaloniki New Experience branch (04/02/2026) and the e-banking/mobile upgrade notice; (2) the investor 'Corporate Presentations' index, which revealed a Corporate Presentation - June 2026 deck the baseline never saw, containing the 'HSBC Malta needs a restart / underinvested in IT' language, the milestone-by-milestone Malta roadmap with TOM completed April 2026, and the branch/FTE rebase; (3) the bank's own New Experience branch locator, giving eight named live sites; (4) Malta Stock Exchange announcement CDN (HSBC474-483 probed) for HSBC Malta primary filings; (5) SEC EDGAR submissions API for Euronet's Q2-2026 8-K, a source environment not used in prior runs, proving the CrediaBank transfer had not closed as at 30/07/2026; (6) Greek local press for the Chania opening. Genuine gaps: the TCR / VTS / branch self-service OEM at CrediaBank is still unnamed anywhere public - searched in Greek and English against Diebold Nixdorf, NCR Atleos, Glory and Printec with no hit, and it remains a standing identification task; likewise the OEM and managed-services holder of HSBC Malta's 2025 Malta/Gozo ATM fleet replacement, and the prime integrator of the digital transformation programme. No 2026 Capital Markets Day webcast transcript is published, only the Greek deck. CrediaBank is a private issuer, so there is no public procurement register to mine (no Diavgeia/Prozorro equivalent).
access_issues: crediabank.com press-office and investor listing pages are JS-rendered and return 0 items to a plain fetch; the /en/ paths are broken (https://www.crediabank.com/en/group/press-office/2026/ returns HTTP 500, /en/group/investor-relations/financial-results/corporate-presentations/ returns 404) while the Greek paths work. Route used: sitemap.xml with a desktop User-Agent to enumerate URLs, then curl each page with the same UA and regex out the /media/*.pdf link, then extract text with pdfminer.six in a local venv (pdftotext is not installed on this machine). Malta Stock Exchange: https://www.borzamalta.com.mt/company-announcements and https://borzamalta.com.mt/company-announcements both 404; worked around via the CDN pattern https://cdn.borzamalta.com.mt/download/announcements/HSBC<NNN>.pdf, probing 474-483 (480 and above return 404, i.e. not yet published). https://www.hsbc.com.mt/investor-relations/ 404s. https://www.euronet.com/newsroom and https://ir.euronetworldwide.com/news-releases both 404 to the fetch tool; obtained the Q2-2026 release instead from the SEC EDGAR submissions API plus the Archives path with a descriptive UA. No source was dropped silently.
